objective: Strengthen Adaptive HACT for journal review with disjoint-seed replication, baseline adequacy, and distribution-shift robustness without changing the v5 primary claim after observing outcomes.
baseline: Original-order compact balanced tree under the existing byte contract.
hypotheses: H1: validated learned ordering reduces held-out padded evidence cost on clustered completion waves across all three registry sizes.
H2: the learned method exceeds marginal-frequency and validated-random-order baselines on clustered completion waves.
H3: incumbent fallback limits false-positive deployment on independent and global controls.
H4: a layout learned before a latent cluster permutation shift loses value, while retuning on post-shift data restores a material fraction of the oracle-order benefit.

statistics.interval: percentile 95% bootstrap interval for the seed-level mean

baselines.learned: Average-linkage order from pairwise Jaccard affinity, compact balanced 8-ary tree; validation chooses between this proposal and incumbent.
baselines.marginal: Descending marginal completion-frequency order with the same balanced tree; validation chooses between this proposal and incumbent.
baselines.random_validated: Incumbent plus eight independently sampled random orders; validation chooses with incumbent-favoring ties.
baselines.oracle_latent: Generator latent cluster order with the same balanced tree; ceiling diagnostic only.
baselines.validation_ablation: Always deploy the learned proposal, omitting the validation/incumbent fallback.

non_goals: No claim of live-LLM quality improvement.
No provider token or billing claim.
No post-hoc seed or baseline replacement after results are observed.
